replies.author: @davidowens1424
replies.text: That's a false.  It's one of the things he was wrong about in his books.  His idea of liabilities and assets assumes that there is a no cost option, and there isn't.  Housing costs something no matter what and owning a house can reduce the housing cost below the expected cost for housing making it an asset.  For example, what's better?  Making an extra $100 per month or reducing your expenses by $100 per month.  Also, in his books things like 'food' and 'health care' would be liabilities.  He has some interesting ideas that are worth hearing, pondering, and building on.  But his system is far from ideal.
